content: Diabetes mellitus encompasses a group of metabolic disorders characterized by the improper processing of glucose, resulting in elevated blood glucose levels, or hyperglycemia. Type 1 Diabetes is primarily an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the insulin-producing beta cells of the pancreas, leading to little or no insulin production. Type 2 Diabetes is commonly associated with insulin resistance, where the body's cells do not respond effectively to insulin, combined with a progressive decline in insulin secretion by the pancreas. Gestational Diabetes refers to a form of diabetes that develops during pregnancy, typically resolving after delivery, but it may increase the risk of developing type 2 diabetes later in life. Other Specific Types of Diabetes arise from identifiable causes, such as genetic mutations affecting beta-cell function, diseases of the pancreas (e.g., pancreatitis), or the use of certain medications that impair glucose metabolism.
